title: Numbers, promotion, overflow and exactness
outcome: Choose and validate numeric representations while distinguishing exact arithmetic, overflow and floating-point approximation.

exercises.title: Retain a remainder
exercises.task: Compute quotient and remainder for 7 divided by 2.
exercises.expected: The integer quotient is 3 and remainder 1.
exercises.answer: Integer division answers another question from floating-point division.

exercises.title: Reject a narrowing conversion
exercises.answer: A constructor conversion that cannot represent the value must not be confused with wrapping arithmetic.

exercises.title: Keep an exact ratio
exercises.answer: This preserves the intended ratio instead of first rounding decimal-looking binary floats.

exercises.title: Choose a precision
exercises.expected: Their types are Float32 and Float64.
exercises.hint: Literal syntax is part of the contract.
exercises.answer: More precision changes representation cost and error; it does not validate the model.

exercises.title: Check a large integer
exercises.expected: The mathematical integer is retained beyond the machine Int range.
exercises.answer: Converting a wrapped machine result afterward cannot reconstruct the lost value.

exercises.title: Explain a tolerance
exercises.task: Justify an absolute tolerance for a measured quantity.
exercises.expected: The bound uses that quantity units and required accuracy.
exercises.hint: Do not substitute a larger bound for a diagnosis.
exercises.answer: Representation, conditioning and algorithmic error inform a tolerance; passing an arbitrary bound proves little.
